# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section B lines 1–25 | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**3:1** And-concerning the offering of-grain of-the-Gentiles which they [...] and-defile the temple: one-should-not eat it.

**3:2** [...] and-one-should-not bring any of-the-grain of-the-Gentiles into the temple, and-one-should-not [...] from-the-Gentiles.

**3:3** For [...] it is not pure, and-it defiles the purity of-the-temple and-the-offerings [...]

**3:4** [...] and-concerning the Gentiles [...] they sacrifice to [...] and-we say that-they-sacrifice to-the-idols [...]

**3:5** And-concerning the sin-offering that-is-cooked in-copper-vessels [...] whereby they-defile [...] the flesh of-their-sacrifices.

**3:6** They should-cook them in-earthen-vessels [...] and-not in-copper-vessels [...]

**3:7** [...] for the copper absorbs [...] the flesh of-the-sin-offering that-is-cooked in-it [...]

**3:8** [...] and-one-should-not cook the sin-offering in-copper, for [...] it renders-impure [...]

**3:9** [...] and-concerning the vessels of-copper [...] they-defile the flesh [...]

**3:10** And-concerning the purity-regulation of-the-cow of-the-sin-offering — the red heifer: the one-who-slaughters-it and the one-who-burns-it and the one-who-gathers its ashes and the one-who-sprinkles the water of-purification —

**3:11** all of-these should-be pure at-sunset, so-that the pure-one sprinkles upon the impure.

**3:12** For the sons of-Aaron should [...] be-careful [...] concerning these things [...]

**3:13** [...] and-not defile themselves [...] for the purity of-the-[red]-heifer [...]

**3:14** [...] and-the-one-who-sprinkles the water of-purification: he-should-be clean [...]

**3:15** [...] for [...] the sons of-Aaron [...] and-concerning this we-have-written to-you [...]

**3:16** And-concerning the skins of-cattle and-sheep [...] one-should-not bring their skins into the temple [...]

**3:17** [...] and-one-should-not [...] any skin [...] that-has-not-been-prepared [...]

**3:18** [...] for [...] the skins [...] defile the purity of-the-temple [...]

**3:19** And-concerning the skin of-the-carcass of-a-clean-animal: the one-who-carries it shall-be-unclean until evening.

**3:20** [...] and-one-should-not bring into the temple any skin [...] from an-unclean-animal [...]

**3:21** [...] and-concerning the bones [...] and-the-hooves [...] one-should-not bring them into the holy place [...]

**3:22** [...] for [...] the purity of-the-temple is above all [...]

**3:23** And-concerning [...] the slaughter that-is-done outside the camp [...] one-should-bring the blood [...]

**3:24** [...] and-pour-it-out [...] upon the base of-the-altar of-burnt-offering [...]

**3:25** [...] for the blood is the life [...] and-it-shall-not be eaten [...]

---

*EMET notes: Section B opens with halakhic disputes over sacrificial purity. The prohibition of Gentile grain offerings in the temple reflects strict separationism. The ruling on copper vs. earthen vessels for cooking sin offerings reflects the view that copper absorbs impurity — a halakhic position at odds with the Pharisaic ruling. The red heifer (parah adummah) regulation at 3:10–15 is critical: the authors insist all participants must wait until sunset for purity, contra the Pharisaic position allowing immediate sprinkling. "At-sunset" (ba-shemesh) is the key halakhic marker. Skin regulations (3:16–22) extend temple purity to animal hides. Hyphenated forms throughout preserve Hebrew construct-chain syntax.*
